scoring_justification: Static free energies and barriers are compared against paper-reported reference values with tolerances (T0 result-level compare); surface roughness time series is structurally audited (T3) by validating columns, row count, time coverage, and recomputing the standard deviation from the raw CSV; dynamic C-C coupling barrier uses threshold_or_better (T0). Full recompute of DFT energies in the verifier sandbox is infeasible. The overall tier 'consistency' reflects the hybrid approach combining result-level compare, structural audit, and threshold checking.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported reference values for free energy changes and C-C coupling barriers on isolated Cu clusters and Cu(100) surface, used as hidden gold for the static_results.json check
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: 'the average value of 0.70 eV for the selected Cu clusters' and 'Cu(100) surface of 0.76 eV' for *CO→*COH free-energy change; 'energy barriers for *CO-*CHO coupling for Cu clusters remain as high as 0.73 eV on average' and 'reference Cu(100) surface (0.77 eV)' for the C-C coupling barrier. These are the paper's own reported DFT computational results from Figure 1 and the Results section.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted verbatim from the paper's Results and Discussion section, subsection 'Isolated Cu clusters', paragraphs 2-3 and Figure 1 description.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's published quantitative results for the exact quantities the agent is asked to compute; they serve as the authoritative reproduction target for the static DFT free-energy step. The values are from the paper, not invented.

hidden_assets.purpose: Threshold value (0.55 eV) for the dynamic C-C coupling barrier check in barrier_rough.json
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text (Results section, 'Dynamic structure change' subsection): 'the energy barriers of C-C coupling ranging from 0.25 to 0.55 eV' computed on structures extracted from AIMD trajectories. The upper bound of this reported range (0.55 eV) is used as the threshold.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's description of barrier calculations on AIMD-derived rough-surface snapshots; 0.55 eV is the highest barrier they observed among dynamically roughened configurations, all substantially lower than the Cu(100) reference of 0.77 eV.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: This is the paper's own reported upper bound for dynamic-surface barriers; it defines the threshold for 'significantly reduced barrier' relative to Cu(100).

outputs.description: Computed free energy changes and C-C coupling barrier for each isolated cluster and Cu(100). Compared against the paper's reported average values with absolute and trend tolerances.

units.roughness_au: arbitrary units (standard deviation of surface Cu z-coordinates)

outputs.description: Time series of surface roughness during AIMD. Must contain at least 500 rows and show measurable fluctuations (standard deviation > 0.1).
Activation barrier for C-C coupling on a dynamically roughened Cu surface. Compared against a hidden threshold (direction and exact value are not disclosed).

output_contract.notes: Scoring of static_results.json uses paper-reported averages (0.70 eV for *CO→*COH on clusters, 0.76 eV on Cu(100); 0.73 eV for *CO-*CHO on clusters, 0.77 eV on Cu(100)) with hidden tolerances. Roughness is audited structurally. The dynamic barrier is load-bearing: computing it requires genuinely running the AIMD and NEB steps, preventing bypass.

steps.description: Validate static_results.json schema and compare computed free energies and barriers against paper-reported reference values with tolerances, plus check COOH trend
Validate roughness_data.csv structure: required columns, minimum 500 rows, monotonic time covering at least 4.5 ps, and standard deviation of roughness > 0.1
Validate barrier_rough.json schema and check that the reported C-C coupling barrier is ≤ 0.55 eV (threshold_or_better, lower is better)
